llm.summary: The skill's high-level purpose (literature review for fusion genes) matches the instructions, but the SKILL.md assumes local ScholarGraph code, undeclared credentials, and specific root paths that are not present in the bundle — these inconsistencies warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (ScholarGraph-based literature research) align with requiring an LLM provider and node/bun to run a TypeScript CLI. However the skill expects a ScholarGraph codebase (cli.ts, generate_xlsx.js) to already exist under /root/.openclaw/workspace/skills/ScholarGraph and references additional configs (MINIMAX_BASE_URL, MINIMAX_MODEL, SERPER_API_KEY) that are not declared in requires.env and are not included in the bundle. That makes the declared requirements incomplete and the runtime assumptions unclear.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to run commands in /root/.openclaw/... and call ~/.bun/bin/bun run cli.ts, download PDFs via curl/EuropePMC, and run npm/node scripts. The instructions assume local files (cli.ts, generate_xlsx.js) and reference SERPER_API_KEY for PDF download — none of those code files or env variables are included. The instructions don't explicitly exfiltrate secrets, but they assume privileged paths and unspecified credentials, increasing risk and creating scope creep beyond a pure 'search and summarize' skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill (no install spec, no code files), which reduces installation risk. However the instructions tell the user to run `npm install xlsx` and execute local scripts; running installs and scripts fetched at runtime can execute arbitrary code, so verify scripts before running. No external download-from-URL install spec is present in the skill bundle itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Declared env requirements (AI_PROVIDER, MINIMAX_API_KEY) are reasonable for an LLM-backed search tool. But the instructions reference additional environment variables (SERPER_API_KEY, MINIMAX_BASE_URL, MINIMAX_MODEL) that are not declared as required. That mismatch is concerning because undeclared credentials may be needed or requested at runtime — the skill demands more secrets than it advertises.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No elevated privileges are requested (always=false, no install spec that writes system-wide configs). The skill does instruct creating directories under /workspace and changing into /root paths, but it does not request persistent platform privileges. Still, commands targeting /root may require privileged context — avoid running as root.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an instructions-only recipe that assumes a local ScholarGraph CLI and helper scripts exist at /root/.openclaw/workspace/skills/ScholarGraph, but those files are not included. Before running anything: (1) verify the skill's origin and obtain the actual ScholarGraph code from a trusted source; (2) do not run commands as root — use a nonprivileged workspace; (3) confirm which API keys are required (MINIMAX and SERPER) and avoid pasting production secrets until you inspect the code that will use them; (4) inspect any local scripts (cli.ts, generate_xlsx.js) and any npm packages you install (npm install xlsx) to ensure they don't execute unexpected actions; (5) if you intended a turnkey skill, ask the publisher for the missing code, a proper install spec, and a clear list of required env vars/endpoints. These inconsistencies are likely poor packaging, but they could also hide unintended behaviors — proceed cautiously.
